name: 993 front impact support, AlSi10Mg graded-core concept F0
description: Independent front support concept with an elliptical shell and a graded open cruciform core, used to screen the value of LPBF AlSi10Mg. PorscheFanatics corroborates the lightweight FVD support at 145 g; FVD publishes a 139 x 100 x 53 mm envelope and states only aluminum, with no alloy and no interface geometry.

classification.intended_use: CAD, mass, stability, energy and DfAM screening only; manufacture, fitting, driving and impact testing prohibited without an approved crash program

provenance.record_license: MIT for the concept, the script and the calculations; no photograph, trademark, illustration or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - lightweight 993 front bumper support
sources.notes: Corroborates the FVD product name, its front left/right position and 0.145 kg; no geometry and no crash validation. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-LIGHTWEIGHT-BUMPER-SUPPORT.

sources.title: FVD - 993 aluminum front impact support
sources.notes: Commercial claims of 139 x 100 x 53 mm, about 145 g and aluminum; direct access blocked during collection, no drawing and no protocol. See SRC-FVD-993-FRONT-IMPACT-TUBE-DIMENSIONS.

sources.title: EOS Aluminium AlSi10Mg material page
sources.notes: Process and material-family reference, not a crash allowables card and not evidence of the FVD alloy. See SRC-EOS-ALSI10MG-CURRENT-PAGE.

material.grade: generic screening AlSi10Mg; alloy and temper of the FVD product unknown
material.standard: ASTM F3318 and a program-specific crash specification to be contracted if LPBF is retained

post_processing: complete powder removal through the four open channels
stress relief and heat treatment qualified on representative coupons
build plate cut-off without initiating cracks in the crush walls
interface machining only after measurement and addition of machining stock
deburring without removing the folding triggers defined by the future calculation
galvanic and corrosion protection to be defined with the bumper and the body shell
supplier_requirements: traceable powder, machine, parameters, orientation, batch and recycling
capability demonstrated on a 1.2 mm shell and a core graded down to 0.8 mm
coupons in the part orientations with quasi-static and dynamic tensile tests
distortion simulation, support strategy and recoater check before launch
CT of the shell and the core, full metrology and dye-penetrant inspection after finishing
quasi-static and dynamic force-displacement curves on representative batches
subsystem then vehicle validation by a qualified crash engineer

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Galvanic compatibility of AlSi10Mg with the body shell, the bumper, the fasteners and the coatings to be qualified.

known_limits: Only the 139 x 100 x 53 mm envelope, the 145 g mass and the aluminum family are published; any F0 topology is hypothetical.
No hole or boss is modeled because no body shell or bumper interface has been measured.
The 144.65 g of the STEP, close to the commercial 145 g, is a designed scalar check, not a geometric validation.
The 15 kN over 80 mm load case and its 6.55 km/h equivalent are synthetic and match no regulatory procedure.
The elastic and plate calculations predict neither progressive folding, fracture, impulse, intrusion nor occupant protection.
The STEP proves only a computable BREP; any manufacture, installation or road use is prohibited at this stage.
